category.item: Meadow
Many grasses, flowers, and juicy clover grow on a nice varied meadow.
Water
Water is not only the home to fish, but also a habitat for many species of birds and mammals.
Ice
Penguins and polar bears are not the only ones to like cold climates, the arctic fox will also enjoy ice and snow!
Savanna
Zebras, wildebeest and bison as well as rhinos and elephant all love to roam the savanna's fertile land. On the other hand, lions and leopards hunt their prey here.
Desert
Animals like lizards, snakes and spiders feel at home in the extremely hostile environment of the desert. Nevertheless, gerbils, desert foxes and wild camels have also found a way to adapt perfectly.
Rocks
Rocky regions are not rich in water nor vegetation. However, rocks do retain heat, which is perfect for poikilothermic animals such as lizards or snakes!
Bamboo grove
Bamboo is the only food for pandas and grows mainly in Asia.
Swamp
The damp and smelly swamp is a great environment for many animal species.
Tundra
Tundra, also known as taiga, is a transitional zone between the frozen lands of the Arctic and the northern coniferous forests. It is home to reindeer, arctic foxes, and arctic hares.
Snow
Many animals feel good in the snow, especially those with thick fur.
Wasteland
Wastelands are created when nature is destroyed by influences such as salt, oil, or the use of technology. Life is hard for animals here, so animals and plants support each other.
Rainforest

Leaf insect, creeping plants and flying snakes - that's life in the jungle! Many animals eat only one type of plant, while the others spend all their life in the trees. Adventure waits for everyone who gets through the bushes!
Terrarium
Reptiles, amphibians and arachnids feel at home in a terrarium. Some are active in the day, others in the night, but all are picky. Terrariums require a lot of care!
Alps
The highest European mountain range is home to brown bears, eagles, wolves, lynxes, and ibex. Animals that prefer cold conditions are threatened by climate change.
Cave
A cozy cave offers not only protection from predators, it also has the same temperature in the winter and in the summer. Bats and amphibians like deep caves to roost in during the winter.
Forest
Many inconspicuous animals hide in the forest thickets. They are wild cats, owls, mice, deer or woodpeckers. It is a life that people often don't even notice when walking in the forest.
Coast
The coast is the boundary between land and water. As a result, there are a number of interesting animals that have adapted to life on both land and water.
Magic mushroom habitat
Look at those little mushroom caps peeking out of the ground... and what is it? A troll? Don't be surprised if something truly wondrous happens in this magical enclosure.
Sugar land
Yum, yum, yum. Lots of sweet tooths are flocking to Sugar Land. Everything there is simply delicious. Who's that munching on the fence?
Ice mass
Water is a liquid with very unusual properties. The ice that floats on the surface of the water acts as a blanket against freezing. This allows marine animals to live even in the coldest seas.
Pool
